$comment: The measured cost of the stricter TypeScript project (tsconfig.strict.json), and the
baseline it may not rise above once somebody has measured it.
`accepted: null` is the honest state and not an oversight: tsconfig.strict.json says in its
own words that what must not happen is a ratchet baseline invented without running it, and
nobody has run it yet. So `npm run typecheck:strict:check` REPORTS today — it prints the
count and the clusters and exits 0 — and becomes one-way the moment the first measurement
npm run typecheck:strict:report                     # how bad is it, and how clustered?
npm run typecheck:strict:accept -- --reason "…"     # pin what it measured
After that a change that ADDS strict errors fails the check. The count may fall and may not
rise (ADR-0007 · AGENTS.md § amber — never raise a ratchet you could have lowered).
